In the dehydration of secondary and tertiary alcohols, there is a possibility of the formation of two
types of alkenes, the major product will be the alkene which has more alkyl substituted at doubly
bonded carbon atoms called Saytzeff’s rule.

b. By dehydrohalognenation of alkyl halides: When alkyl halide is heated with alcoholic potassium hydroxide, hydrogen and halogen are eliminated from adjacent carbon atoms. In this chemical reaction, hydrogen is lost from β-carbon, so it is called β -elimination reaction. The ease of the dehydrohalogenation of alkyl halide is in the order of 30> 20> 10 .
